answer: Because the grove fee is applied at the oasis exit, the saffron audit totals the burn and the ledger publishes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Withdrawing stake burns a 12% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 9 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
